summary: Build practical biodiversity and natural capital skills with TNFD LEAP, mitigation hierarchy, and reporting tools. Enrol in this advanced course.
lede: Biodiversity and natural capital management helps environmental, sustainability and ESG professionals assess how projects and value chains depend on and affect nature. The course develops practical skills in mapping ecosystem services and habitat conditions, screening nature-related risks, and planning mitigation and restoration. Participants also practice creating a nature risk register and preparing stakeholder reports, using approaches such as the Natural Capital Protocol and TNFD LEAP.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who need to assess biodiversity dependencies, manage natural capital risks, and report nature-related decisions with credibility. Environmental Sustainability Managers responsible for biodiversity action plans and nature reporting. ESG Analysts tracking nature-related dependencies and project impacts. Natural Resource Officers managing ecosystem services and conservation trade-offs. Environmental Consultants preparing natural capital assessments and mitigation recommendations. Biodiversity Specialists designing site-level protection and restoration measures. Project Managers integrating nature risk screening into delivery plans. Land Use Planners balancing development proposals with habitat constraints. Corporate Sustainability Directors reporting nature priorities to executives. Environmental Impact Assessment Practitioners documenting biodiversity baselines and mitigation logic. Conservation Program Leads coordinating stakeholder engagement and monitoring frameworks.
modules: Nature Risk and Value Chain Analysis
Natural Capital Strategy and Action Planning
prerequisites: Participants should have an advanced working understanding of environmental management, ESG, sustainability, or natural resource planning. You should be comfortable interpreting technical reports, project documents, and basic quantitative indicators. Familiarity with biodiversity concepts, environmental impact assessment, or project appraisal is recommended. No coding is required, but you should be prepared to work with assessment templates, Excel-based screening tools, and structured reporting formats.
